description: Orbital Forge is a space-focused engineering team interested in orbital mechanics, satellite systems, mission analysis, and scientific software. Our experience includes flight dynamics, trajectory modeling, perturbation analysis, orbit determination, Python, C, SPICE, and data visualization. We aim to turn real space data into practical, technically grounded tools for exploration and mission planning.
summary: LunarNav is an offline Windows app for comparing landing sites and dates near the Moon’s south pole. Users can select a site on an interactive map or enter coordinates, then see where the Sun and Earth appear relative to the local horizon. LunarNav uses NASA/JPL ephemerides and lunar elevation data to estimate sunlight and direct Earth visibility over time. Side-by-side comparisons help users see how a change in landing location or date affects both visibility windows.
details:
LunarNav lets users choose a lunar location, a UTC start time, and an analysis duration. It displays the Sun’s and Earth’s azimuth and elevation and estimates when each is visible above the local horizon. Users can switch between a flat horizon and a terrain-based horizon to see how ridges and crater rims affect visibility. A timeline shows changes over the selected period, and saved scenarios let users compare locations and dates side by side.

The Windows app runs offline. It uses NASA/JPL Horizons reference data and SPICE kernels for astronomical positions, LOLA elevation data for terrain horizons, and LROC and NASA Moon Trek imagery for the lunar maps. Canadian Space Agency material provides context for Earth-operated lunar rovers. The application was built with React, TypeScript, Three.js, Electron, Python, and FastAPI. OpenAI Codex assisted with coding, testing, and documentation.

Visibility estimates use the centers of the Sun and Earth. The timeline estimates transitions between hourly samples. These estimates help compare lighting and communication opportunities. Electrical output and radio link performance require additional analysis.
